items.scenario: You open a Sentry issue for E202 (the SoundFont failed to load) to see whether it only happens in Safari. Yet every visit's Release Health ping did send the full user-agent string, which the home page's description of the ping leaves out.
items.corrections: None in the claims. Precision: with `{ allow: ['User-Agent'] }` the Referer is not removed — its key stays on the event with the value `[Filtered]` (Sentry keeps key names). "Neither header can carry an IP address" holds for the visitor's address; the Referer holds the linking page's address.
items.notes_for_triage: Option 1 is the reviewer's recommendation (ADV-2, the only contributor). Withholding the Referer matters: a same-origin referrer can hold the previous page's query string (`fbclid`), which §3.1's address scrub does not cover. Option 2's cost: no browser, OS or device on any issue, and Sentry's crawler and legacy-browser filters cannot match error events (sessions are still filtered). Both options must fix §3.4: the ping sends the user agent whatever `dataCollection` says. A third path, proposed by no reviewer and untested: strip it in a `client.on('beforeSendSession', …)` hook (core/src/client.ts:618, 758) — then the crawler filter no longer applies to sessions and bot visits count in the health number. The ping also carries a random per-page-load id (`sid`), start and update times and an error count; no `did` (no user is set) and no IP. Separate from this item: every error event also carries the visitor's locale and time zone (`contexts.culture`, on by default), which §3.1 does not list (also the adversarial reviewer's residual risk); add a row, or filter out `CultureContext` too. The home copy's "only" clause is about the file, so it stays true under both options.

  is sent (`beforeSend`), the filter runs over each exception's message, and over nothing else.

- `reportError`: the default level, the `code` tag, and E101–E103 dropping the message;
